title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly sync on Redwood Private VPC pilot. Discussed networking updates (peering, route tables, egress IPs), routing for model traffic, certificate/ingress plans for on-prem control plane, a minor upgrade schedule for runtime, and next perf tests. Action items include network diagram, egress IP list, updated upgrade plan and next benchmark run.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-13 10:00 PDT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Toni (Redwood CSM), Lisa (HavenHealth), Marcus (HavenHealth infra), Priya (HavenHealth security), Darren (product)

[00:00] Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining for the weekly POC sync. can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Lisa: yep, loud and clear.
[00:05] Marcus: good morning.
[00:07] Morgan: quick agenda — networking status, routing and ingress, upgrade window for the runtime we're testing, perf results from last run, and action items. if anything else we should add?
[00:12] Priya: security questions later about audit logs and key management.
[00:15] Samir: i'll lead through the technical bits; i pulled logs and the perf sheets.

[02:00] Samir: ok first, networking — last week you had the cross-account VPC peering in progress, any updates on the peering and route tables?
[02:12] Marcus: yes, we got the peering created yesterday but we hit a routing issue. the route table for the private-subnet wasn't propagating the redwood CIDR, so traffic to the inference workers was being dropped. turned out to be a small typo in the route entry.
[02:30] Marcus: fixed that, and we can now reach the control plane endpoints from the bastion. we still need the egress IP list to add to our outbound firewall allow list.
[02:38] Morgan: right, i'll send the egress IPs. note that for the pilot we recommend reserving the three static egress IPs we provided in the doc — that avoids NAT hairpin issues.
[02:48] Lisa: one thing — are those egress IPs per-cluster or per-region?
[02:52] Samir: per-cluster by default. if you want region-level aggregated egress we can provide a NAT gateway pattern but you'll want to consider the single egress point for audit.

[05:10] Priya: from security perspective, we also need to know TLS termination — are you doing TLS at the LB in our VPC, or is the control plane terminating?
[05:20] Morgan: current default is TLS from the client to the control plane; for Redwood Private we let customers terminate TLS on their side — the control plane also supports mTLS and cert pinning if you want mutual TLS.
[05:34] Priya: good. we need details for SSO and cert rotation cadence.
[05:38] Toni: we'll share the SAML metadata and the cert rotation doc after this meeting.

[07:00] Darren: on the routing question — we saw some 503s during the last load test. i think they correlated with the model variant fallback. can you explain what happened?
[07:12] Samir: yes, during the 99th percentile spike we observed model A hitting memory limits. the runtime automatically fell back to a quantized variant which increased CPU pressure and caused a brief backlog in the router. there was a short window of 503s for about 30 seconds.
[07:30] Morgan: that's expected behavior for the current canary policy. we can tweak the fallback threshold or pre-warm the quantized variant to avoid cold starts.
[07:40] Marcus: is there a way to pin a route to only use dedicated instances? we want to avoid fallback during critical traffic.
[07:46] Samir: yes, you can set routing policy to prefer dedicated pool and disable automatic fallback for that route. i'll propose a config example in the doc.

[10:05] Samir: performance numbers — last run with the 2.7B model quantized to int8 we saw p50 token latency ~45ms, p95 ~210ms under 200 concurrent qps. throughput peaked at about 650 tokens/s per GPU in your cluster shape.
[10:25] Lisa: those numbers look promising. what was the batch size and KV cache config?
[10:30] Samir: batch size was 8, dynamic batching enabled with a 50ms max wait, KV cache warmed for warm-start tests. for cold start the p95 jumped to 420ms.
[10:40] Morgan: to reduce cold-starts we suggest enabling persistent KV caching and the pre-warm policy we discussed. that reduces cold-starts to under 150ms in our benchmarks.

[12:15] Marcus: on the infrastructure side we also need to confirm our subnet CIDR won't overlap with the control plane overlay — you mentioned an overlay 10.240.0.0/16?
[12:24] Samir: yes the control plane overlay is 10.240.0.0/16 by default. we can change it if you have conflicting ranges.
[12:30] Marcus: we do have 10.240.0.0/20 in our prod VNets, so we'll need to update.
[12:36] Morgan: noted — i'll include the overlay config options in the network diagram update.

[15:00] Priya: regarding audit logs and retention — we need logs forwarded to your SIEM and retention for 365 days. what options do we have?
[15:10] Toni: for Private deployments we offer direct S3 export or streaming to your syslog/SMTP — sorry, syslog or Kinesis. we'll share the doc. retention is configurable on your side; Redwood will keep operational logs for 30 days unless you enable long term export.
[15:30] Priya: ok export to S3 with lifecycle is fine, we just need the schema for the logs.

[17:05] Darren: upgrade question — you said there is a minor runtime upgrade to the serving runtime that resolves a KV cache leak, what's the risk window?
[17:16] Samir: the patch is small; we tested in staging. upgrade is rolling per-node and should be non-disruptive, but we recommend a 30-minute maintenance window to allow for canary and quick rollback if needed.
[17:28] Morgan: for the pilot we can schedule the upgrade overnight in your time zone. if you want zero impact we can do a canary on a small subset first.
[17:36] Lisa: overnight window works. can you share the exact steps and expected timing?
[17:40] Samir: yes — step doc + rollback steps, and we'll include the telemetry checks we watch during the upgrade.

[20:00] Marcus: one more note — our infra team prefers the control plane to use private DNS; can you confirm you support Split-horizon DNS?
[20:08] Samir: yes split-horizon is supported. we'll provide the internal hostnames and zone files you can import.

[22:00] Morgan: quick review of the perf action items — we'll run another benchmark with the quantized model but pre-warmed cache and batch size 12 to see the latency/throughput tradeoff. target to run mid next week.
[22:12] Samir: i'll set up the benchmark and post results to the shared spreadsheet. expect charts for p50/p95/p99 and token throughput.

[25:00] Lisa: a question on data residency — for this pilot are model logs ever stored outside our VPC?
[25:08] Morgan: no, in Redwood Private the control plane metadata can be configured for your VPC-only export. content is never stored outside unless you opt into logging to Redwood hosted analytics.
[25:20] Priya: good to confirm. please add that to the compliance note we asked for.

[28:00] Darren: can you also share the recommended canary config for model rollouts? we want an A/B style traffic split and automatic rollback on quality regression.
[28:12] Toni: yes there's a rollout doc that includes canary percentages, automatic rollback triggers by error-rate and latency, and example configs. we'll attach it.

[30:30] Morgan: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[30:35] Morgan: action — send full network diagram with overlay CIDR options and egress IPs (Morgan).
[30:42] Morgan: action — run follow-up perf test with pre-warmed KV cache and batch size 12, share results (Samir).
[30:48] Morgan: action — share SAML metadata and cert rotation cadence doc (Toni).
[30:52] Morgan: action — HavenHealth to confirm internal security approval and provide SIEM export destination (Priya).
[31:00] Morgan: action — schedule upgrade window and share step-by-step plan (Samir + Morgan).

[33:00] Priya: timeline-wise we aim to complete network and security approvals by end of next week, then perform the runtime upgrade and perf run the following week. does that align?
[33:08] Lisa: yes that fits with our release calendar.

[35:00] Samir: quick note about costs — using dedicated pool with pinned routes will increase cost but gives predictable latency. we'll follow up with a short cost estimate for the pinned route config.
[35:12] Morgan: we'll attach a short cost spreadsheet and example tradeoffs: dedicated vs hosted fallbacks, quantization savings.

[37:00] Marcus: any blockers from Redwood on the networking side?
[37:06] Samir: no blockers — just need the final CIDR choice and we'll update the overlay. once we have the egress IP allow list we'll confirm connectivity and run a smoke test.

[40:00] Lisa: thanks everyone. one last ask — can you provide a short summary email with the checklist and docs?
[40:08] Morgan: yes we'll send a summary with links to the network diagram, rollout doc, cert rotation, and the perf spreadsheet.

[42:00] Toni: thanks all, see you next week.
[42:05] Darren: thanks.
[42:08] Morgan: thanks folks. bye.

End transcript.
